text:
Maya (PM): Quick note from the post-launch desk: we need a lightweight, repeatable flow for the first week. Goal: fix high-impact regressions fast, keep small improvements moving, and avoid derailing next sprint. Draft below — please annotate.

Jon (Eng): Love the idea of a lightweight flow. Can we codify decision gates? Example: Impact x Reach -> immediate (same-day) / short-term (3-day) / backlog. Impact = user-facing correctness, Reach = % of requests.

Pri (SRE): Concrete thresholds help. Propose: Immediate = either (a) user-facing failure + >1% traffic OR (b) any enterprise customer error. Short-term = issues seen by >0.1% or repeated user reports. Backlog = everything else. I'll add auto-tags when error-rate crosses these levels.

Lena (Design): For short-term UX polish, I can do micro-mocks and acceptance tests. Suggest we require a design sign-off for anything that touches primary flows.

Maya (PM): Process suggestion: 1) Morning quick triage (10-15m) -> tag Immediate/Short-term/Backlog 2) Immediate -> page oncall + freeze unrelated merges to `release/*` 3) Short-term -> owner + 1 dev pair for a single-day patch window 4) Backlog -> queue for Friday grooming. Also add PR size guideline for triage patches: <= 120 LOC and include `rollback:` header in PR body.

Jon (Eng): Rollback header is smart. Also: model-serving infra changes get mandatory canary (3-5%) and a 15-minute observation window with `p50/p95/p99` and error-rate checks. UI fixes can go behind a feature flag for staged release.

Pri (SRE): I'll own canary orchestration. Runbook checklist for Immediate fixes: reproduce -> test vector -> owner -> write patch + unit tests -> canary -> monitor 15m -> promote/rollback. If patch ETA > 4h, escalate to on-call lead.

Maya (PM): Customer escalations: tag with `[ENTERPRISE:<customer>]` in ticket title and loop CS + AM immediately. If it's on Dedicated infra, we treat as Immediate by default.

Lena (Design): I will attach 2 variants per short-term UX fix: quick patch vs safer revert. Include acceptance criteria: success path + smoke test steps.

Jon (Eng): I'm taking first Immediate if anything shows up in the next 6h. Spinning a branch off `release/2026-03` for any hotfixes. ETA for patch PR: ~2.5h.

ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled by Jon: hotfix/1919191919 -> canary(4%) at 1919192005

Pri (SRE): Alerts wired to #prod-watch. I'll post the minimal runbook template in #runbooks (repro, metrics to watch, rollback cmd).

Maya (PM): Friday groom: move accepted Backlog items that are <=3 dev-days into the next minor wave and assign owners. Bring 3 customer follow-ups and 2 quick UX wins. Reconvene 3pm today for status.

Jon (Eng): Sharing quick repro for a failing path: `POST /v1/complete` with empty `input` sometimes returns 502; stack points to `response_mux.cpp`. Ticket created and linked.

Pri (SRE): Got it — correlating with a surge from region-eu this morning. Will include that in the incident note.

Maya (PM): Thanks team. If anyone needs more real-time help, ping me directly. :raised_hands:
